study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Coupé et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2022
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Hippocampal-amygdalo-ventricular atrophy score: Alzheimer disease detection using normative and pathological lifespan models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Low-order polynomial regression (linear, quadratic, cubic) for lifespan trajectories; model selection via ANOVA significance tests and BIC.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: - Linear model - Quadratic model - Cubic model; Afterwards, to select the most relevant model between these potential candidates, we used the Bayesian Information Criterion (Schwarz, 1978).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: MRI-derived structure volumes, including hippocampus/amygdala and inferior lateral ventricle volumes, plus tissue segmentations for GM/WM/CSF.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: After a full screening of the most discriminant structures between AD and normal aging based on MRI volumetric analysis of 3,032 subjects; These structures are combined to create tissue segmentations (gray matter [GM], white matter [WM], and cerebrospinal fluid [CSF]); we decided to combine the volume of hippocampus, amygdala, and inferior lateral ventricle to propose a novel HAVAs.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Coupe2022.pdf.md: Abstract; Coupe2022.pdf.md: 2.2 | Image processing; Coupe2022.pdf.md: 2.5 | Classification using volume trajectories

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Lifespan trajectories modeled with linear, quadratic, and cubic age terms.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: For AD detection, volume or thickness of key structures as a function of age is usually used.; To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: - Linear model - Quadratic model - Cubic model
